reading.body:
This notes, knowledge, and meetings category is the largest in this dataset with 29 tools, spanning meeting transcription and recording, Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, Fathom, Grain, tldv.io, general productivity and project management with AI layered in, Asana, ClickUp, Monday.com, Trello, and personal or team knowledge bases, Notion, Obsidian, Logseq, Mem, NotebookLM.

A recurring "consent relevant" or "consent and privacy" note appears specifically on the meeting recording and transcription tools, Fireflies.ai, Otter.ai, Fathom, Grain, and tldv.io, distinguishing them from the broader productivity tools in the same category, since recording a conversation and transcribing it raises a distinct legal question, whether every participant consented to being recorded, that a task management AI simply does not carry.

Jurisdiction varies meaningfully within this one category: Logseq and Obsidian are built around local first, no cloud dependency privacy design as a core feature, while most of the remaining tools operate as cloud services subject to their vendor's own data governance, and a handful, Confluence and Trello from Atlassian in Australia, tldv.io in Germany, Monday.com in Israel, are flagged for jurisdiction specific data transfer considerations.

The data does not include adoption figures, pricing, or how consent requirements for the meeting recording tools are actually enforced in practice across different jurisdictions, so whether these 29 tools are being used in compliance with the consent norms their own notes flag is not established by this record.
